source.title: Inferring Functionality of Attention Heads from their Parameters

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests recurrence of interpretable attention-head operations across language models using vocabulary-space relation scores and head counts, rather than measuring representational distance or alignment.
record.gate_note: The study tests V5 at the level of relation-defined attention-head operations recurring across LLMs. Its head-output correlations and causal ablations validate MAPS estimates and their behavioral relevance, but do not measure cross-model representational alignment. It does not test scale-dependent convergence, paired image-caption alignment, interchangeable representations, or alternative similarity metrics.
record.test_reason: In §4.4 and Tables 6–7 the study counts heads implementing 20 token-pair relations in 6 LLMs from four families, and compares relation-score distributions across models (Figure 3). This bears on V5 in a new setting: interpretable attention-head operations read from parameters, not SAE features or neurons. Universality is a side analysis of a method paper, so T3 fits better than T2. It does not measure representational alignment, so V1–V4, V6 and V7 are untested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors say several relations are encoded to similar maximum degrees across models despite architecture and data differences. They read this as supporting the universality hypothesis of Li et al. (2015). They also find each relation spread across many heads at varying strengths, not localized, and describe architecture biases: smaller models pack more relations per head, and grouped heads in Llama share relations.
record.recipe_differences: Uses vocabulary-projected attention-head parameters and relation scores or head counts; it does not measure representational similarity between models as in the convergence claim.
record.method_sensitivity: In the head-output correlation experiments, correlations can change between inputs with and without context; the paper notes larger drops for some relations and models. The relation-score procedure also uses different top-k settings for different model families.

fits_no_version.finding: The share of heads implementing relations from several categories falls with model size: 38% in GPT-2 xl, 11% in Llama-3.1 70B. Grouped-query attention in Llama makes grouped heads implement the same relations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architecture and scale change how universal operations are distributed across heads, even when the operations themselves recur.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics, 2024
record.problems: The evidence is about selected relation-defined operations in language-model attention heads, not representational-distance convergence or identity of features across models. Model families use different tokenizers and top-k settings, and the reported cross-model comparisons cover only a subset of relations and models.
record.rows_left_out: No other reported result directly measures cross-model recurrence relevant to V5. Head-output correlations, causal ablations, and the salient-operation analysis validate or characterize MAPS but do not measure cross-model representation alignment.

untested.parts: There is no measure of cross-model alignment or of its change with scale. Models of several sizes are compared only by head counts.
No mapping, stitching or relative-representation tests between models.
Recurrence of individual neurons, SAE features, or identical circuits or bases is not tested. Only relation-level operations of attention-head OV matrices, read in vocabulary space, are tested.
No comparison of similarity metrics or out-of-distribution inputs. Thresholds and top-k were tuned per model family but not varied systematically for the cross-model comparison.
No test of whether shared data or objectives explain the recurrence.

missing.what: Per-model head counts for all 20 relations, including copying and country-to-capital, and the near-zero word-to-last-letter and homophone counts in all models.
Per-model maximum relation scores, which quantify the 'similar degrees' claim of Figure 3.
Random-initialization baseline: 0 heads classified in five models and 5 of 1200 in GPT-2 xl, versus 250 trained GPT-2 xl heads.

record.verdict_notes: Cross-model comparisons use different k values (Llama 3/25 vs 1/10), different tokenizer-filtered datasets, and first-MLP preprocessing applied to every model except Llama 70B. So head counts and scores are not strictly matched across models. The method reads parameters (W_VO in vocabulary space), not activations; recurrence is of relation-level functions, not of shared representations.

versions.untested_parts: No measure of alignment between independently trained models or of how alignment changes with model size or capability.
No vision-language models or paired image-caption representations.
No same-architecture, different-initialization comparison or shared-subspace analysis.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired alignment test between model representations.
Tests recurrence of relation-defined attention-head operations, not identity of individual units, exact circuits, or matching feature bases.
No comparison of representation-similarity measures or systematic test of convergence under alternative metrics or out-of-distribution inputs.
Does not assess whether cross-model alignment is incomplete or plateauing, or whether shared data or objectives explain recurrence.

relation.reason: The study supplies its own cross-model measurements of recurring interpretable attention-head operations and explicitly evaluates function universality.

tranche.reason: Section 4.4 directly investigates the same universality question named by V5, using a different method: vocabulary-projected parameters, relation scores and head counts. This fits different method, same question.

source_check.notes: MAPS measures vocabulary-expressible output operations, not complete circuits; token-pair datasets and top-k settings differ by tokenizer/model. Statement checks cover only this study; corpus totals and other cited studies cannot be independently checked from the permitted files.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: The relation-defined attention-head operations reported across the tested LLMs
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports several relations appearing in many of the six models and similar relation-score distributions across four models; see R1–R8. This supports recurrence at the level of mapped head operations, not identity of individual units or circuits.
